dataset.title: Dataset- ADIMAG - Additive Manufacturing and Smart Surface Engineering of Magnesium

dmp.description:
Mg and its alloys are becoming increasingly important for transport and biomedical applications. Their excellent strength-to-weight ratio and high damping capacity are exploited in automobiles and aircrafts components, whereas their low elastic modulus, biocompatibility and bioresorbable properties are desirable for temporal implants. Both sectors demand technologies that enable manufacturing of customtailored components of complex geometry with high precision. It is in this context where additive manufacturing (AM) comes through as a forerunner.
AM is a disruptive technology that enables direct fabrication of computer-aided designs which are unattainable by conventional metalworking processes. AM also offers an unparalleled on-site lean manufacturing approach with a unique combination of flexibility and environmental perspective. Currently, AM of Mg alloys is almost exclusively limited to small facilities and only in a handful of countries, of which Spain is not one. Another limitation is the extremely small range of available Mg-based systems suitable for AM technologies. These shortcomings are due to the high reactivity of Mg powder and its tendency to evaporate. Regardless of the application, AM alloys inevitably require surface engineering solutions providing corrosion protection and other functionalities (wear resistance, biocompatibility, etc.). This is particularly important for Mg as its high corrosion rate in many environments is one of its main limitations for wider industrial use. However, surface engineering of AM alloys is a new field that remains virtually unexplored in case of AM Mg alloys.
The main objective of ADIMAG is to develop AM Mg alloys and smart environmentally friendly surface technologies specifically designed for transport and biomedical applications. The project will deliver rational use of raw materials with reduced energy losses, processing times and costs in combination with added surface functionalities such as active protection, bioactivity and smart drug release. This will contribute to the transition towards climate neutrality and digital leadership as change accelerators, thus reinforcing the strategic autonomy of the industry in regards to materials and manufacturing technologies. Therefore, ADIMAG is aligned with the Strategic Line New materials and fabrication techniques (Thematic Priority 4, PEICTI 2021-2023) and with Cluster 4: Digital, Industry and Space (Pillar II, Horizon Europe).
The strategy of the project will be based on three pillars:
1) Design, Simulation and AM of Mg-based components by laser powder bed fusion. Alloy composition, processing parameters and building strategy will be adapted for the particular needs of transport and biomedical applications.
2) Smart surfaces by laser treatment, thermal spraying, plasma electrolytic oxidation, layered double hydroxides, sol-gel and polymeric layers. Enhanced corrosion protection and bioactivity will be achieved through the combined use of inhibitors/drugs and hybrid coatings with hierarchical architectures.
3) Systematic characterization and evaluation of the developed materials and surface finishes, with particular emphasis on corrosion, wear, mechanical and cytocompatibility tests.
URJC and UCM groups have experience on AM alloys and their surface modification. Their long-standing collaboration in the field of light alloys and complementary research facilities provide the necessary tools to tackle the project.

This DMP is a part of WP1 (Coordination, Management and State of the Art) in the ADIMAG project. The purpose of this DMP is to describe the data management strategy (data handling, data sharing, data privacy and data ownership). Relevant links with data from the project are included in the DMP.
